newsitem.title: INDIA: India says studying reported Chinese infiltrations.
newsitem.headline: India says studying reported Chinese infiltrations.

text.p: Indian officials said on Wednesday that they were studying reports of recent Chinese troop infiltrations across the Himayalan borders dividing the two countries.

Foreign Minister Inder Gujral told parliament that newspaper reports of at least six Chinese intrusions into the northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh between February 4 and 18 were "very serious", the United News of India (UNI) said.
"As far as we know the border has been very peaceful with no reports of any armed incidents in recent years," a foreign ministry official said.
"We have a good mechanism in place to sort out any misunderstandings on the spot. So we have to study what these reports are," the official told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
Himachal Pradesh, one of five Indian states bordering China, is also home to the Dalai Lama, the exiled spiritual leader of China's Tibet region.

UNI said two deputies of the rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) who raised the issue in the upper house of parliament had charged that Indian troops guarding the borders had shown white flags to their Chinese counterparts.

"We want to know why the Chinese troops were not attacked," BJP deputy Vijay Malhotra asked. He said Chinese troops had entered Indian territory previously too without any retaliation from the Indians.
Indian diplomatic sources said such occurrences were rare but said Indians were also involved in straying into the other side.
India and China fought a brief border war in 1962.
Their relations thawed in 1988 when then Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi visited Beijing for talks with Chinese officials.
The two countries signed a treaty of "peace and tranquillity" along their borders in 1993.
